source.title: Towards Theoretically Understanding Why SGD Generalizes Better Than ADAM in Deep Learning
source.authors: Pan Zhou; Jiashi Feng; Chao Ma; Caiming Xiong; S. Hoi; E. Weinan

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary text are present. The extracted text has PDF conversion artifacts in some equations and names, but the relevant experimental results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares SGD and Adam on natural-label classification and measures gradient-noise tails, using its own theory and experiments to explain the generalization gap. This is a conceptual test of V4 and V7; the cited optimizer comparisons are prior work, not this study's results.
record.gate_note: Rows cover this study's own CIFAR10 AlexNet gradient-noise comparison and its MNIST/CIFAR10 fully connected SGD-versus-Adam results. Prior-work claims cited in the introduction and related work are not rows. Tail-index trajectories and barriers in Figure 4 are described qualitatively; no precise values are reconstructed from the figure.
record.test_reason: The study's own SGD–Adam comparisons measure training and test accuracy on MNIST and CIFAR-10 and bear on V4. Its gradient-noise and basin-escape analyses do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' explanation. Under their assumptions, their Lévy-driven SDE analysis predicts faster basin escape for SGD than Adam because of noise structure and geometry adaptation; they also discuss learning-rate differences. They interpret this as explaining SGD's better generalization by connecting larger-basin minima to better test performance through prior work. Their experiments support the noise assumptions and predicted behavior, rather than independently establishing that causal connection.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares standard SGD and Adam in experiments, but its central explanation uses Lévy-driven SDE analysis and basin-escape theory rather than directly testing the optimizer recipes or tuning conditions in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported optimizer gap differs by dataset: it is small on MNIST and larger on CIFAR10. The gradient-noise tail index varies over optimization iterations; the authors describe some iterations where SGD's tail index is much smaller than Adam's.

fits_no_version.finding: AlexNet gradient noise on CIFAR-10 is heavy-tailed, fits an alpha-stable distribution better than a Gaussian, and has heavier tails for SGD than Adam.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer gradient-noise distributions differ in tail heaviness during image-classifier training.

record.problems: The optimizer comparison is reported for only MNIST and CIFAR10 fully connected networks, with no stated uncertainty estimates. Noise-tail evidence is presented mainly through figures and qualitative descriptions; no exact tail-index values are supplied in the text. The paper's generalization explanation relies on theoretical assumptions and links to flat or asymmetric minima whose generalization properties are cited from prior work.
record.rows_left_out: No required results omitted. Figure 4's tail-index trajectories and possible barriers are described qualitatively and not entered as numeric rows because the text gives no precise values. Results in Figure 6 compare algorithm and SDE convergence trajectories but do not measure a claim version's named outcome.

untested.parts: Matched random-label memorization and natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local-connectivity interventions.
The learning-rate and decay tuning protocol is unspecified. Broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, other adaptive optimizers, and language benchmarks are not tested.
Large-batch penalties under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based predictors.
Removing memorized examples and retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. A small MNIST accuracy difference does not itself qualify V4, which specifies no minimum effect size. No uncertainty estimates establish the reliability of either reported gap.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization capacity and natural-label generalization under matched recipes are not tested.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold is not swept.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization is not compared; the AlexNet experiment only measures gradient noise.
The study compares SGD with Adam on MNIST and CIFAR10, but does not test broader optimizer tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, or word-level language models.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to large-batch training are not tested.
Dropout and weight-decay interventions are not tested.

The paper does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- or margin-based gap predictors. Its basin measure and gradient-noise tail index are proposed as explanatory factors, but are not the V7 measure.
Memorized-example removal and retraining are not tested.
